question: Three-fifth of a journey is covered at a speed of 84 km/hr, and the remaining distance is covered at the rate of 56 km/hr. The average speed for the whole journey (in km/hr) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total distance be 5 units, divided into 3 units and 2 units.

Time for the first part = Distance ÷ Speed = 3 ÷ 84 = 1/28 hours.

Time for the remaining part = Distance ÷ Speed = 2 ÷ 56 = 1/28 hours.

Total time taken = 1/28 + 1/28 = 2/28 = 1/14 hours.

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 5 ÷ (1/14) = 5 × 14 = 70 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed for 3/5 of the journey = 84 km/hr

Speed for the remaining journey = 56 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 3/5 Distance
 
 

 2/5 Distance
 
 Speed = 84 km/hr
 Speed = 56 km/hr

 Time = (3/5 D) / 84
 Time = (2/5 D) / 56

 Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total distance of the journey be D.

⇒ Distance covered in the first part = 3D / 5

⇒ Remaining distance = D − (3D / 5) = 2D / 5

⇒ Time taken for the first part = (3D / 5) ÷ 84 = 3D / 420 = D / 140

⇒ Time taken for the remaining part = (2D / 5) ÷ 56 = 2D / 280 = D / 140

⇒ Total time = (D / 140) + (D / 140) = 2D / 140 = D / 70

⇒ Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Average speed = D ÷ (D / 70) = D × (70 / D) = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (General Concept)

Average speed over a journey is defined as the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken, not the simple arithmetic mean of the speeds.

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If a person covers two equal halves of a journey at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by the formula: (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction at speeds x and y (where x > y), their relative speed is (x − y). If they move in opposite directions, it is (x + y).
